This page walks through creating a bot, getting its token, and inviting it to a server. It takes about two minutes.

Open Settings → Bots in Disband (or the Developers portal) and click New bot . - Give it a name. The name is what appears in the member list and on messages. - Pick the scopes it needs. Start small — you can always create another bot with more scopes, or edit them later. The full list is on the bots overview. - Click Create . Disband returns a token , shown

From the Developers portal, click Edit on your bot to set: - Avatar URL — profile picture (any HTTPS image). - Banner URL — banner image for the bot's profile. - Bio — a short description shown on the bot's profile. - Scopes — add or remove permissions.

Any machine that can make outbound HTTPS requests works. Since the gateway is long-polling (your code holds a connection open, and Disband returns events when they arrive), you do not need a public address, inbound ports, or a websocket. The gateway loops forever on its own; it reconnects and retries automatically. Three things tend to kill real bots: 1. Crash loops. Wrap the client in a supervisor and restart on failure: 2. Stale tokens. If the bot is revoked (or an invite expires before it is approved), the gateway API returns 401 . Handle it: log clearly and stop, rather than retrying for
Bots only talk to the scoped HTTP API. To poll or persist state, use any storage you already operate — a file, a database, Redis — the client does not care.

A bot can be invited to many servers. The approved scopes are per server, so a bot that can read messages everywhere is also only ever writing where the owner granted messages.write . Your code can branch on message.server id if the behaviour needs to differ per server.

Every request sends: Header Value Authorization Bot Content-Type application/json A missing or invalid token returns 401 { "error": "Invalid bot token" } . A revoked bot returns the same, so a 401 means "check the token" — not "retry". All endpoints are scoped: a bot can only read or write what its scopes (and the per-server grants) allow. A bot's reach in a space is the intersection of: 1. the scopes chosen on the bot account, and 2. the scopes the space owner approved for that bot. Lowering an account scope immediately trims it from existing space grants. Adding it back does not restore the old grant; the bot must be approved again. Every endpoint uses the bot token: A missing, invalid, or revoked token returns: with status 401 . There is no unauthenticated read path in this API.

A bot has an account-level scope list chosen when it is created (and editable by its owner), plus a per-space grant approved when the bot joins that space. The effective scopes are the intersection of the two. Lowering a bot's account scopes applies immediately: the removed scopes are trimmed from every existing space grant. Disband's status page is self-hosted. It does not depend on a third-party status service, so it can still report accurately when the main web host, API, or stat

The page groups monitors by service. For each monitor it shows: - the current state from the latest check; - the HTTP status and response time of that check; - a 90-day uptime bar, one segment per day; - the last time a check ran. Below the monitors are incidents, scheduled maintenance, and announcements. Each opens a detail page with the full update timelin

Automated checks run every minute and record one result per monitor. A monitor is healthy only when its expected HTTP status matches and any configured keyword is present. Timeouts, network errors, wrong statuses, and missing keywords are recorded as failures. Checks run independently of the web app, so a failure at the web host does not stop checks being re

Each check is stored and rolled up into daily history, so the 90-day uptime bar is read from precomputed data rather than aggregated on demand. - Raw checks are retained for 90 days. - Daily roll-ups are retained for 180 days. - The public page displays the latest 90 days. - Each day's segment is the percentage of successful checks that day.
